scheme_name: Subsidy Scheme For Establishment Of 100 Broiler Birds' Farm For Schedule Caste
description:
The Subsidy Scheme for Establishment of 100 Broiler Birds' Farm for Scheduled Caste was launched by the Government of India to promote entrepreneurship among Scheduled Caste communities.

This scheme was initiated in the year 2018 under the Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying.

The primary objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance to Scheduled Caste individuals to establish a broiler farming business.

The scheme aims to enhance the income levels of Scheduled Caste families by promoting self-employment opportunities in the poultry sector.

The target is to establish 100 broiler birds' farms in each district across India.

The scheme is designed to empower Scheduled Caste individuals by providing them with the necessary resources to start their own businesses.

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is up to INR 1.5 lakh per beneficiary.

This amount covers the cost of infrastructure, equipment, and initial feed for the birds.

The scheme also aims to create awareness about modern poultry farming techniques among the beneficiaries.

Eligibility criteria for this scheme include being a member of the Scheduled Caste community.

Applicants must be at least 18 years old to qualify for the subsidy.

There is no upper age limit specified for applicants.

The income limit for beneficiaries is set at INR 1 lakh per annum.

This income limit ensures that the scheme targets economically weaker sections of the Scheduled Caste community.

The application process for the scheme requires interested individuals to approach the nearest Animal Husbandry Department office.

Applicants must fill out a prescribed application form available at the office.

Required documents include a caste certificate, income certificate, and identity proof.

Additionally, applicants must provide a project report detailing the proposed farm's layout and operational plan.

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the officials at the Animal Husbandry Department.

The review process typically takes about 15 to 30 days.

If approved, beneficiaries will receive the subsidy amount directly into their bank accounts.

The subsidy is disbursed in two installments.

The first installment is released upon the approval of the application.

The second installment is released after the successful establishment of the farm.

The timeline for establishing the farm is generally set at six months from the date of receiving the first installment.

The scheme is implemented through the State Animal Husbandry Departments.

Each state has its own designated officials responsible for overseeing the implementation of the scheme.

Beneficiaries can contact the local Animal Husbandry office for assistance and guidance.

The scheme is part of the larger initiative to promote entrepreneurship among marginalized communities.

The government aims to increase the production of poultry in India through such initiatives.

According to the National Livestock Policy 2013, poultry farming is identified as a crucial sector for rural development.

The poultry sector contributes significantly to the agricultural GDP of India.

As of 2021, the poultry sector accounted for approximately 4.5% of the total agricultural GDP.

The scheme also aligns with the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana and other welfare schemes aimed at uplifting the socio-economic status of Scheduled Castes.

The government has set a target to establish around 10,000 broiler farms across the country under this scheme.

This initiative is expected to create thousands of jobs in the rural economy.

The scheme promotes sustainable farming practices by encouraging the use of modern technologies.

Training programs are also organized for beneficiaries to enhance their skills in poultry management.

The government collaborates with various NGOs and institutions to provide training and support.

The subsidy scheme is part of the broader strategy to achieve self-sufficiency in poultry production.

The poultry industry in India is expected to grow at a CAGR of 10% over the next five years.

This growth is driven by increasing demand for poultry products among consumers.

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of biosecurity measures in poultry farming.

Beneficiaries are encouraged to adopt best practices to ensure the health and productivity of their flocks.

The government provides guidelines on the construction of poultry houses and feeding practices.

The scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries who have successfully established their farms.

Many beneficiaries have reported an increase in their household income as a result of the scheme.

The government regularly monitors the progress of the scheme through field visits and assessments.

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the implementation of the scheme.

The scheme is expected to contribute to poverty alleviation in rural areas.

The government aims to create a sustainable livelihood for Scheduled Caste families through this initiative.

Overall, the Subsidy Scheme for Establishment of 100 Broiler Birds' Farm for Scheduled Caste is a significant step towards empowering marginalized communities in India.

It provides a structured framework for individuals to engage in profitable agricultural activities.

The scheme not only aims to improve individual livelihoods but also contributes to the overall growth of the poultry sector in India.

In conclusion, this scheme represents a vital effort by the Indian government to enhance the socio-economic status of Scheduled Caste communities through entrepreneurship in poultry farming.
